Laura —

Thanks for the clear recap. Below are answers from Finlys security + DevOps. I also attached our standard compliance questionnaire (finlys_compliance_questionnaire.xlsx) with additional context.

Answers to your bullets:
- Retention windows: Primary logs (indexable metadata and pseudonymized IDs) = 30 days. Cold archive for investigations = 180 days (we keep hashes/indices only, not full payloads) unless Legal requests otherwise.
- Request/response bodies: Default: do NOT persist full request/response payloads. We require that any PII fields (names, SSNs, payment tokens, personal identifiers) be redacted at ingestion. For a small set of transactional records (payment dispute flows) we do allow storing masked payment references (last 4 digits) if stored encrypted and access-controlled.
- Headers & trace IDs: We want to persist a short set of headers for debugging (User-Agent, Content-Type, X-Env, X-Redwood-Route). X-Forwarded-For must be truncated to /24. For trace IDs, we prefer storing a deterministic hash (SHA-256) of the trace id + a per-customer salt so we can correlate across services without exposing raw values.
- Data residency: EU-only for logs and any persistent redaction artifacts for EU customers. Our legal team requires that raw payloads never persist in non-EU regions.
- KMS: BYOK preferred for logs and archived artifacts; must integrate with our HSM-backed KMS.

Open questions for Redwood:
1) Can Redwood perform regex + pattern-based redaction at ingest (server-side) before any data is written to persistent logs?
2) What is the expected latency impact of in-flight redaction? We need a ballpark for tail latency increase.
3) Can trace ID hashing be done deterministically within Redwood so our debugging workflows still work across services?

We are happy to join a workshop. Our availability: Aug 4–6, mornings (CET).

Thanks,

Hi all —

Thanks Anika, and thanks Laura for the ping. Below is a proposed approach from Redwood SE + engineering to meet Finlys requirements. High level first, then the specifics that map to your bullets.

Proposed approach (summary):
- Ingest-time sanitization pipeline: a streaming sanitizer component running on the customer plane (Hosted option with EU-region nodes OR Dedicated/Private install) that applies a rule-set (regex + allowlist) and policy-driven redaction. The sanitizer runs before any persistent logging write.
- Trace ID handling: compute a deterministic HMAC-SHA256(trace_id, customer_salt) at ingest and store only the hash in logs. Salt is stored in the customer's KMS (BYOK) and never leaves the customer's control for Private/Dedicated. For Hosted EU customers we propose storing salt in an EU key vault.
- Headers and truncation: persist only a configured header allowlist. X-Forwarded-For will be truncated to /24 at ingestion.
- Request/response bodies: default behavior will be to strip full payloads from persistent logs. For allowed transactional records (payment dispute flow), we will persist a masked/minimized record (e.g., last4 + encrypted reference) behind RBAC.
- Retention: default 30 days for indexable metadata and hashed trace ids; archival indices (hashes only) for up to 180 days. All retention settings configurable per-customer.
- KMS/BYOK: support for customer-managed keys using HSM-backed KMS (Azure Key Vault / AWS KMS with external key material) for any encrypted artifacts.

Estimated impact to latency:
- Streaming sanitizer adds ~2–8ms median, with p95 ~30ms and p99 ~120ms in our benchmarks for comparable regex sets. These numbers depend heavily on the number and complexity of regex rules; we will provide a mini-benchmark during the workshop.

Effort estimate (EPIC-level):
- SE configuration & workshop: 2 days (Dylan + Laura prep)
- Ingest sanitizer setup and rule tuning (Dedicated/Hosted EU): 6 days (1 SE + 2 infra engineers)
- Trace hashing + KMS integration: 4 days (1 infra eng + 1 infra architect)
- QA, compliance testing, documentation: 3 days
Total: ~15 engineering days + 2 SE days (spread across 3 weeks for scheduling and validation).

Follow-up asks for Finlys to confirm so we can SOW:
1) Confirm final retention windows (30/180 vs 30/90)
2) Confirm EU-only requirement (true/false)
3) Confirm acceptance of deterministic HMAC of trace IDs (Anika said yes, please confirm)
4) Share sample log lines / 5 representative request payloads (sanitized) so we can tune regex rules.

Attachments referenced: redaction_engine_design.md (high-level design), sample_regex_set.txt (we'll generate after we get samples).

If this aligns, I can convert the EPIC estimate into a short SOW and timeline; happy to run the workshop the week of Aug 4 (CET mornings) as suggested.
